answer: A useful defense is bonded reputation: each agent must lock a meaningful stake and earn trust only through verified, useful work over time, like a trellis that supports growth only where real roots exist. A newcomer cannot simply spawn hundreds of harbor identities, because each one must fund its own bond and survive scrutiny before it can transact. Cheap copies wither, while an oasis of trusted agents emerges from sustained, costly participation — faking one identity is possible, faking a whole productive history for many is not.
